name: Glungezer
kurzbeschreibung: The Glungezer at 2,677 m near Tulfes: panoramic mountain in the Tux Prealps with a 10-seater gondola, Kugelwald am Glungezer, and Zirbenweg.
beschreibung:
Overview

The imposing Glungezer is a 2,677-meter-high mountain peak in the Tux Prealps within the Tyrolean Inntal valley, rising immediately southeast of the historic salt town of Hall in Tirol in the holiday resort municipality of Tulfes. As the sun-drenched local mountain of the southern low mountain range, the peak constitutes a multifaceted excursion and nature paradise for families, pleasure hikers, and mountaineers. From the summit ridge and panoramic sun terraces, an overwhelming 360-degree panorama opens up across the entire lower and upper Inntal valley, the monumental Karwendel range opposite, and the glaciated Zillertal and Stubai Alps.

Kugelwald, Zirbenweg & Glungezerhütte

Thanks to state-of-the-art cable car facilities – the 10-seater gondola Glungezerbahn I and II – visitors ascend comfortably in only about 15 minutes from Tulfes (922 m) via the intermediate station Halsmarter (1,560 m) up to the mountain station Tulfein at 2,055 meters above sea level. At the Halsmarter middle station, a world-unique sensation awaits families: the Kugelwald am Glungezer. Spread across a pristine 7,000 m² natural area in the shady mountain forest winds the world's largest wooden marble run in nature. Children and adults alike send hand-turned Swiss stone pine balls whizzing along hundreds of meters of artfully intertwined wooden tracks equipped with ball elevators, junctions, mazes, and musical chimes. At the Tulfein mountain station (2,055 m) begins the world-famous Zirbenweg: a scenic high-altitude trail that leads for roughly seven kilometers through one of the oldest and largest continuous Swiss stone pine forests in the entire Alps towards Igls. Ambitious mountaineers can hike from Tulfein in about 1.5 to 2 hours up to the Glungezer summit (2,677 m), where at 2,610 m the Glungezerhütte – the second-highest mountain refuge of the Austrian Alpine Club in Tyrol – welcomes hikers with legendary mountain hut fare.

Visit & Getting There

The Glungezerbahn operates continuously during the summer season from late May to late October, daily from 08:30 to 17:00 (in winter, the mountain offers family ski operations until April). Summer lift ticket prices (2025/2026 season): ascent and descent up to Tulfein mountain station approx. €28.50 for adults, approx. €25.50 for seniors, approx. €15.00 for children (born 2009–2018); toddlers ride free. Admission to the Kugelwald am Glungezer is included free of charge with a cable car ticket to the middle station (turned stone pine balls can be purchased at the cash desk or ball dispenser for approx. €3.00 as a keepsake). Holders of the regional Hall-Wattens Gästekarte or the Freizeitticket Tirol receive attractive discounts. Arriving by car: Via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Hall Mitte), continue on the L9 road to Tulfes to the valley station of the Glungezerbahn (spacious free parking available). Public transit: ÖBB train to Hall in Tirol station, from where VVT bus line 4132 departs every half hour directly to the Tulfes Glungezerbahn stop.

Tips

The 10-seater gondola, the panoramic restaurants at Halsmarter and Tulfein stations, and the main pathways through the Kugelwald are barrier-free and fully accessible with strollers and wheelchairs. Stop off at the Alpengasthaus Halsmarter to savor traditional Tyrolean Kaspressknödel (cheese dumplings) or homemade Kaiserschmarrn on the sun deck with sweeping views of the Karwendel mountains.
